cim_eredeti: European stocks fall amid growing concerns over artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
London, Nov. 7 (SANA) European stocks fell by around 1% at the close of trading on Friday, weighed down by widespread losses led by insurance shares, as investors grew increasingly cautious about the outlook for the artificial intelligence sector and political developments in the United States.

Reuters reported that the pan-European STOXX 600 index closed at 648.33 points, while Germany’s benchmark index recorded the steepest losses among European markets, declining by 1.9%.

The insurance sector led the downturn, falling 2.6% after JPMorgan downgraded German reinsurers. Hannover Re shares dropped 4.3%, Munich Re fell 4.4%, and Swiss Re declined 4.6%, despite reporting an increase in net profit.

Technology shares also slipped 0.2%, extending their losses for a second consecutive session. Declines spread to other sectors, with media stocks falling 2.3% and personal and household goods shares losing 1.9%, as investors moved to reduce their exposure to risk.

Among individual stocks, Teleperformance was the biggest decliner, plunging 15.3% after the company lowered its full-year revenue growth forecast.European stocks had also closed lower on Thursday, weighed down by losses in technology shares.
